linkNotes: Use this confirmed 3D camera form. Inputs are {lat} and {lon} in degrees (planetocentric, east-positive Mean Earth frame), and {heightMeters} above the mean lunar sphere. Convert lat and lon to radians phi and lambda. Let R=1737400 m; n=(cos(phi)*cos(lambda),cos(phi)*sin(lambda),sin(phi)); position (x,y,z)=(R+heightMeters)*n; direction (dx,dy,dz)=-n; up (ux,uy,uz)=(-sin(phi)*cos(lambda),-sin(phi)*sin(lambda),cos(phi)). Serialize the nine numeric components followed by 60, comma-separated, into camera, preferably with encodeURIComponent. The final 60 is field of view in degrees; proj=22 selects the 3D lunar globe. Choose a positive height comfortably above local terrain; 100000 m was used in the tests. At the exact pole the longitude sets the north-up orientation. No stack or selectedFeature parameter is needed for a plain destination link. Do not use unconfirmed x/y/z query parameters merely because the SPA returns HTTP 200.

linkEvidence.name: LROC Rimae Hippalus image page; published QuickMap permalink uses this ten-number camera structure
linkEvidence.method: Published camera position, direction, and up vectors numerically match the nadir/local-north formula. Radius and projection id come from the supplied QuickMap catalogue.

catalogue.referenceSystem: Mean Earth (ME); catalogue Moon is a sphere of radius 1737400 m. Layer/source ids are distinct; stack uses layer ids.
catalogue.dataProvenance: Vector dataPath values are copied from sourcesById. The catalogue identifies its own file CDN as the vector-data server; no new vector download was needed. PDS/LROC metadata pages are linked where available.

limitations: Tests establish HTTP response and a camera construction consistent with a published primary-source link; visible browser centering was not checked because the computer-use host was unavailable.
The catalogue’s labels preserve historical mission names and do not prove future mission status. ShadowCam mosaics and general illumination layers are not listed as binary PSR masks.
Do not copy stack from the team reference link: it combines both 2022 and 2024 Artemis region layers and two PSR thresholds.
